newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coal miners form protest chain over subsidies cut.
newsitem.headline: German coal miners form protest chain over subsidies cut.

text.p: About 100,000 miners and supporters formed a 60-mile human chain across Germany's industrial heartland Friday in protest government plans to reduce coal subsidies.

The chain, linking the western cities of Dortmund, Duisburg and Essen, was organised by miners' union IG Bergbau after Finance Minister Theo Waigel, under pressure to trim the budget to qualify for European monetary union, proposed the cuts.
Miners' leaders rejected government proposals to reduce annual coal subsidies sharply from the current total 10 billion marks ($5.9 billion).
Some members of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition partners want to cut the subsidies to 3.5 billion marks ($2.1 billion) and eventually phase them out entirely.
Union leader Hans Berger said the industry needed at least 6.5 billion marks ($3.85 billion) in annual support to stay afloat.
Current law commits Bonn to pay about 7.0 billion marks ($4.2 billion) and state governments to pay 3.0 billion marks ($1.8 billion) in coal subsidies annually up to the year 2000.
